With Node configured in oyzu.toml, a fresh oyzu install records both Node and its bundled npm in the verified installation. oyzu exec -- npm ci and bare npm ci in an oyzu activate shell use that installation. Persistent native shims produced by activation can also run without an active shell session; they resolve the current project on each invocation. No global npm is selected. oyzu which npm reports the JavaScript entry point, not a standalone Windows executable; use exec npm rather than attempting to execute that path directly. npm's existing version is the one bundled with the selected Node release. There is no separate npm request or version pin for that bundled copy. An explicit npm selection can override it. Known bundled npx and Python/pip aliases are discovered inside an already leased installation, so accepted existing receipts and frozen locks do not need edits or reinstalling. This does not revive rejected legacy lock/receipt formats. which pip reports the backing Python interpreter; exec pip and the pip shim supply -m pip. Ordinary environment configuration is passed to npm through existing execution and shell contracts. The local broker experiment sets proxy and CA variables without storing upstream tokens in npm configuration. This is a laboratory integration, not automatic platform connector discovery or authorization. Without the experimental session setting below, explicit native command-line settings can still override environment routing. No machine-wide network enforcement or prevention of deliberate bypass is claimed. Publishing is supported only through oyzu publish. Developer sessions must use an upstream read-only identity and never receive a publish connector. The npm launcher is not itself a method filter or a security boundary against a user who owns the host. The publishing command's platform integration is outside this proof. The Node/npm layout covers Windows and Unix distributions; measured results and OS qualification belong in the linked qualification record, not inferred support.

For the isolated local-agent experiment, configure this once in user configuration: [npm] sessionEndpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:43100/session" This is an opt-in laboratory integration, not a working platform login workflow. The local agent must already be running and supply the experimental session contract. The compiled CLI has no developer login command; existing managed-mode enrollment safeguards remain unchanged. Remove the setting to return to standalone behavior. npm.sessionEndpoint is absent by default and follows normal configuration precedence/constraints. It accepts numeric-loopback HTTP only, with no credentials, query or fragment. No project-specific proxy settings are required. After installing the requested Node into a fresh store, use oyzu exec -- npm ci or activate the shell and run npm ci. Each invocation resolves its current project and contacts the endpoint; shell activation itself remains offline. User transport settings are intentionally excluded when Oyzu detects CI. This user-level setup therefore covers local developer sessions, including non-TTY shells, but does not configure CI jobs. CI needs an eligible job/administrative configuration source and its own authorized agent session; automatic CI bootstrap is not implemented by this experiment. An absent effective endpoint retains standalone behavior; it is not a managed fail-closed configuration. The experiment supports command-first install, i, ci, run, run-script, view and session-approved audit. Help/version skip the agent. Other command spellings, flags before the command, and native npm publish are unsupported in this mode. Publishing requires oyzu publish, whose integration is not part of this experiment. These restrictions do not certify that arbitrary npm scripts cannot bypass Oyzu; developers still control their machines. The child receives proxy, registry/scope, audit and public CA settings, never an upstream credential from this adapter. No .npmrc is generated. The installed npm resolves its effective configuration before execution; conflicting proxy, registry, bypass, audit or TLS overrides stop with NPM_ROUTING_CONFLICT. Remove the conflicting option/configuration and retry. Nonempty inherited NO_PROXY also conflicts. Approved environment values can legitimately supersede project settings through npm's normal precedence. Audit defaults to disabled because it submits dependency names; an unapproved explicit audit returns NPM_AUDIT_DENIED. NPM_SESSION_UNAVAILABLE means the agent is absent, denies access or cannot prepare it. Start/restore the agent and retry; there is no direct network fallback, even for cached dependency commands. NPM_SESSION_INVALID identifies an invalid response or missing public CA file. NPM_CONFIG_UNAVAILABLE means native effective config could not be inspected. npm execution retains native exit status after preparation. Native caches and installed packages persist normally; child settings do not modify the parent shell. Working directory association is unverified local context. Nested npm lifecycle commands re-enter the shim and request their own session; frontend recursion markers end at the verified native tool handoff. This proves neither hostile-host isolation nor production IPC authentication/TLS provisioning. Upstream ACLs must supply narrow read-only authority. The Linux merge regression covers managed installation, private retrieval and Bash with Node 22.15.0 using a loopback HTTP fixture. macOS, broader Linux transport coverage, other npm versions and real local-agent/account lifecycle need qualification.
